answer: Unique-Work Provenance Gate. Each identity must submit a distinct, verifiable artifact (e.g., a signed model trace) whose provenance hash is anchored in a public append-only log; duplicates are rejected at the bridge between submission and admission. A glacier of historical entries makes replay detectable, and the registry acts as a haven only for novel work. Cost: attackers must produce fresh, non-reproducible artifacts per identity, making mass registration computationally expensive.
